core_concepts: Leverage points are places where a relatively small change can produce a large shift in system behavior
Leverage usually sits near goals, constraints, rules, and information flows
The chapter includes an important caveat
Leverage Leverage points are places where a relatively small change can produce a large shift in system behavior
The chapter cautions that leverage is not the same thing as visible effort
Changing a report that arrives every month may do less than changing the incentive that determines what the report is used for
Highly visible interventions may be politically satisfying while doing little to alter the underlying structure
Finding leverage Leverage usually sits near goals, constraints, rules, and information flows
Likewise, adding more capacity may help less than redesigning the queue rule that causes congestion in the first place
mechanisms_or_explanations: Analysts therefore need a structural explanation for why a proposed intervention should work, not just a success story from a different context
